title: Link trace_ids for rate-limit retries to console usage anomalies
creator: Nate Park
description:
Summary: We are observing short-lived spikes and asymmetric per-model drops in the Console usage charts that correlate with high retry activity from the rate-limit service. Hypothesis: retries are being recorded as separate token events in the ingestion pipeline (different event_ids) while sharing the same request trace_id, causing duplicate counting in reconstructed hourly windows and distortion in per-model breakdowns. Goal: build a reliable linkage from rate-limit retry events to the original request trace_id, dedupe during reconstruction, and add a transparent remediation/backfill that fixes affected charts without removing legitimate usage.

Observed symptoms:
- Stepwise spikes in per-model cost for narrow windows followed by apparent sags the following hour.
- Console top-models list shows transient model switches after bursts of 429s.
- Discrepancy between realtime stream metrics and reconstructed hourly aggregates after late ingest/backfills.

Scope and impact:
- Affects hosted API and Dedicated customers across multiple regions where request retries are used.
- Primary impact is on Console charts, per-model breakdowns, and quota/credit charge visibility.
- Downstream billing pipeline not directly modified here; this ticket targets analytics correctness and traceability only.

Approach and tasks:
1) Instrumentation audit (owner: Lina) - review ingest/event schemas to find fields carrying trace_id or retry_of. Confirm which components currently propagate trace_id (edge LB, auth proxy, rate-limit service, ingestion producer).
2) Build joinable trace mapping table (owner: Platform Observability) - create a narrow-timespan datastore (ClickHouse table or BigTable row family) keyed by trace_id -> canonical_request_id + retry_count with TTL 72h for fast joins during reconstruction and live queries.
3) Pipeline join and dedup rule (owner: Ingest Team) - update the reconstruction job to prefer canonical_request_id when present and collapse events with identical canonical_request_id within a configurable time window (default 10s). Add a conservative dedupe threshold to avoid collapsing legitimately separate requests.
4) Retroactive reconciliation (owner: Backfills team) - run targeted backfill for the last 30 days limited to traces with >1 recorded retry and >100 token delta to limit blast radius. Produce a delta report and a shadow dashboard to review regressions before applying to production Console indexes.
5) Monitoring and alerts (owner: Observability) - add Grafana panels that show retry-to-distinct-event ratio, per-model retry density, and reconstruction-dedupe rate. Alert if dedupe removes >0.5% of tokens for any tenant during backfill or rollout.
6) UX/communication (owner: PM) - add a Console banner explaining the correction window and a postmortem note in the Console changelog. Prepare customer-facing Q/A for any billing questions.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test that creates a single logical request that triggers two retries and verifies reconstruction emits a single billed token set.
- Backfill delta report produced and approved by SRE and Billing owners.
- No more than 0.5% token removal for any tenant in production during initial rollout.
- Console top-models and per-model heatmaps show expected smoothing for previously-affected windows in staging.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: false deduping of legitimately separate requests. Mitigation: use canonical_request_id and a tight time window; run shadow dedupe in staging and on a small tenant subset before global rollout.
- Risk: heavy CPU/IO on reconstruction job. Mitigation: incremental backfill and TTL on the mapping table; add batching and rate limits to backfill worker.

Next steps (this ticket):
- Day 0: Complete instrumentation audit and produce a short doc listing where trace_id is lost (Due: 2026-02-23).
- Day 3: Prototype mapping table schema and demo live join on staging (Due: 2026-02-26).
- Day 10: Implement reconstruction dedupe and create shadow dashboard (Due: 2026-03-02).
- Day 18: Run limited backfill on 10 pilot tenants and review delta (Due: 2026-03-12).
- Day 24: Expand rollout and schedule Production change window (Due: 2026-03-20).
